title: Doctor Know-All
lines: There was once a poor man, and his name was Crab.
One day this poor man took a cartload of wood into town and sold it to a doctor.
The doctor was just sitting at the table
when he paid for the wood, and the poor man nearly ate the fine food with his eyes
and the drink that was on the table.
He thought to himself: oh, how well off doctors are!
If only I could be a doctor, then I would live like a gentleman too,
I would eat and drink all day, and no one would be happier than me!
Whatever he thought, he went and asked the doctor:
"Tell me, could I not become a doctor too?"
"Of course you could," answered the doctor.
"Nothing is easier.
First of all, buy an ABC book, that one,
you know, the one with a rooster painted at the front;
sell your ox and your cart, and with the money buy doctor's clothes and everything
that a doctor needs.
Above all, do not forget to buy spectacles.
Then you will look like a real doctor.
Then have a big sign made, and have this written on it:
Here lives the Know-All Doctor. And nail this sign to your gate."
The peasant went home and did everything, to the last letter, as the doctor advised.
And soon the fame of the Know-All Doctor spread across seven times seven lands,
and even a lame step beyond that.
Word went everywhere that Master Crab knew everything,
that there was no secret in the world he could not find out.
No, there was none.
Once it happened that a great lord's money was stolen.
When it could not be found anywhere, someone told the great lord
that in such-and-such a place there was a know-all doctor,
called Crab; he should send for him, and he would tell where the money was.
Well, the great lord did not need telling twice; he had his horses harnessed,
drove to the know-all doctor, went in and asked if what they said about him was true.
"Every word of it is true," said Master Crab.
They agreed at once, and Master Crab was taken to the lord's castle, and his wife too,
and there they were seated at once in the finest room,
the table was laid, and Master Crab and his wife sat down at it.
As they sat down, the first servant brought in a dish, and Master Crab nudged his wife.
"Here is the first."
The servant nearly dropped the dish, he was so frightened.
He thought the know-all doctor meant: here is the first thief.
And indeed he was a thief, and so were the other servants.
The servant went out and said to the others: "We are done for!
The doctor knows everything.
As I came in, he said to his wife: that is the first!"
The second servant did not want to go in at all, but he had to go in all the same.
As he came in with the dish, Master Crab nudged his wife:
"This is the second!"
It was a wonder of God that the servant did not drop the dish, he was so frightened.
"We are done for," he said outside, "this man really does know everything.
When I came in, he said: this is the second."
The third one fared just the same.
The fourth servant had to carry in a covered dish; the lord went in too,
because he wanted to test whether the doctor knew what was in the dish.
Oh, how the poor doctor sweated,
he scratched his head, and in his misery he sighed: oh, poor Crab!
"That's right," said the lord with great joy, "there really is crab in it.
Now I believe that you know where the money is, too."
The lord went out, and the servants came at once, called out the doctor, surrounded him,
and confessed that the four of them had stolen the money;
they would give him a share, if only he did not give them away.
They even showed him where they had hidden the money.
With that Master Crab went back into his room.
The lord was there again and asked: well, what news, doctor?
Master Crab sat down at the table, took out his ABC book,
pushed his spectacles up on his forehead and said:
"I will look it up in this book at once."
Meanwhile, so I don't forget, the fifth servant had hidden in the stove,
for he wanted to hear whether the doctor really knew everything.
Master Crab began to turn the pages back and forth, looking for the rooster picture.
For a long time he could not find the rooster, and he angrily struck the book.
"I know you are in here, you must come out."
The fifth servant thought he was talking about him,
he jumped out of the stove in terrible fright and cried: He really does know everything!
Then Master Crab shut the book and led the lord to the place
where the servants had hidden the money,
and the lord paid him well, and the servants paid him well too,
he could hardly carry it all, he got so much money.
So it was, it is over, it was a tale.
Whoever does not believe it can go and see for himself.
